claims.claim_text: Mission Technology Solutions (MTS, formerly Government Solutions) generated $5,581 million in fiscal 2025 revenue (~72% of $7,786M total consolidated revenue) primarily serving U.S. DoW, intelligence community, NASA, U.K. MoD, and Australian defense customers.

Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) generated $2,205 million in fiscal 2025 revenue (~28% of total), up 2% from $2,155M, anchored by 85+ proprietary process technologies in ammonia/syngas, petrochemicals, clean refining, and circular-economy verticals.

U.S. government represented $4,427 million (57%) of fiscal 2025 consolidated revenues and U.K. government represented $663 million (9%); no other customer exceeded 10% threshold. U.S. government accounts receivable concentration is 47% of consolidated AR.

KBR derives significant MTS revenue from U.S. intelligence community customers including National Reconnaissance Office, National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, and 'other intelligence agencies' under classified work requiring cleared personnel and facility clearances.

Cyber analytics and cybersecurity are described as a core MTS capability area; KBR positions itself in 'cyber analytics, cybersecurity, space and air dominance, connected battlespace, national security intelligence' work for DoW and IC customers.

Backlog of unfulfilled orders was $16,864 million as of January 2, 2026 (up from $16,605M y/y), with approximately 36% expected to convert to revenue in fiscal 2026 and 17% held within equity-method joint ventures (Aspire Defence, Affinity/MFTS, JKC, KZJV).

Defense modernization, national security space superiority, and hypersonics test & evaluation are named strategic growth vectors and KBR claims long-term programs in defense modernization and space superiority funded by U.S. DoW and allied governments.

KBR's MTS growth in fiscal 2025 was driven by the August 2024 LinQuest acquisition (defense and intel programs) and the May 2025 Infrastar acquisition; offset by 'reduced activity within the European command and science and space programs' indicating organic MTS revenue shrinkage ex-M&A.
